pages.text: Selina’s class was visiting a rainforest reserve in southern Ghana. The trees were taller than the school. Mr Ntim, the guide, gave three rules: stay on the path, stay with your partner, and if you are ever lost, stop and stay where you are.
sentences: Selina’s class was visiting a rainforest reserve in southern Ghana.
The trees were taller than the school.
Mr Ntim, the guide, gave three rules: stay on the path, stay with your partner, and if you are ever lost, stop and stay where you are.
pages.alt: A school group stands at the edge of a path in a tall rainforest with a guide.

pages.text: Selina’s partner Ebo loved photography. When a blue butterfly landed beside the path, he tiptoed after it. Then another. ‘Ebo, wait!’ Selina followed him. When she looked up, the path had vanished.
sentences: Selina’s partner Ebo loved photography.
When a blue butterfly landed beside the path, he tiptoed after it.
Then another.
‘Ebo, wait!’ Selina followed him.
When she looked up, the path had vanished.
pages.alt: A boy with a camera follows a butterfly into thick forest while a girl follows.

pages.text: The forest looked the same in every direction: trunks, vines, leaves. The thick leaves high above, called the canopy, blocked most of the sun. ‘Which way did we come from?’ asked Ebo. ‘I do not know,’ said Selina. Her heart began to pound.
sentences: The forest looked the same in every direction: trunks, vines, leaves.
The thick leaves high above, called the canopy, blocked most of the sun.
‘Which way did we come from?’ asked Ebo.
‘I do not know,’ said Selina.
Her heart began to pound.
pages.alt: The children stand in dim green light among identical tree trunks, looking worried.

pages.text: Ebo wanted to run. ‘Wait,’ said Selina. She remembered Mr Ntim’s rule, and a word to remember: STOP. Stop moving. Think. Observe. Plan. ‘If we wander, we get more lost,’ she said, ‘and the group will search along the path.’
sentences: Ebo wanted to run.
‘Wait,’ said Selina.
She remembered Mr Ntim’s rule, and a word to remember: STOP.
Stop moving.
Think.
Observe.
Plan.
‘If we wander, we get more lost,’ she said, ‘and the group will search along the path.’
pages.alt: The girl holds up her hand to stop the boy from running.

pages.text: They counted what they had: one bottle of water, two biscuits, a whistle on Ebo’s bag and Selina’s bright orange raincoat. Selina tied the coat to a low branch. ‘Now we are easier to see,’ she said. ‘The plan: three short whistle blasts, then listen.’
sentences: They counted what they had: one bottle of water, two biscuits, a whistle on Ebo’s bag and Selina’s bright orange raincoat.
Selina tied the coat to a low branch.
‘Now we are easier to see,’ she said.
‘The plan: three short whistle blasts, then listen.’
pages.alt: The girl ties an orange raincoat to a branch while the boy counts supplies.

pages.text: Pheep, pheep, pheep! They listened. Insects hummed. Far above, branches crashed as monkeys moved. Nothing else. They waited a few minutes and blew again. They sat close together on a log, took small sips of water and breathed slowly to stay calm.
sentences: Pheep, pheep, pheep!
They listened.
Insects hummed.
Far above, branches crashed as monkeys moved.
Nothing else.
They waited a few minutes and blew again.
They sat close together on a log, took small sips of water and breathed slowly to stay calm.
pages.alt: The children sit on a log; one blows a whistle while the other listens.

pages.text: On the fourth try, they heard a faint answer: three whistles, far away. Then a voice: ‘Selina! Ebo!’ ‘Here!’ they shouted, and blew again. Mr Ntim’s torch beam found the orange raincoat first. ‘Good raincoat,’ he said.
sentences: On the fourth try, they heard a faint answer: three whistles, far away.
Then a voice: ‘Selina!
Ebo!’ ‘Here!’ they shouted, and blew again.
Mr Ntim’s torch beam found the orange raincoat first.
‘Good raincoat,’ he said.
pages.alt: A guide with a torch appears between the trees, lighting the orange raincoat.

pages.text: On the path, Mr Ntim said, ‘You did the right things: you stopped, stayed put, made yourselves easy to find and stayed calm.’ Ebo apologised. ‘Next time, photos from the path,’ he said. Selina looked up at the huge trees. ‘The forest is not our enemy,’ she said. ‘It is just very big, and we must respect it.’ The end.

pages.alt: The children walk back to the group on the path with the guide behind them.

activities.question: What was Mr Ntim’s rule about being lost?
options: Stop and stay where you are

activities.prompt: Ebo wants to run, but Selina says to stop. What do you think will happen if they wander?
options: They will find the path quickly

activities.question: Why did Selina tie her orange raincoat to a branch?
options: To make them easier to see
To mark a path to the road

activities.definition: The roof of leaves and branches high up in a forest.

activities.prompt: Put the children’s survival steps in order.
Selina’s heart pounded, but she stayed calm. What helps you stay calm when you feel afraid?

glossary.definition: The roof of leaves and branches high above a forest floor.
A small tool that makes a loud, high sound when you blow it.
Look carefully and notice what is around you.
